anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description: Definition: Root cause located in the lock-manager layer, where concurrent transactions request mutually incompatible row, key-range, page, table, metadata, or advisory locks on the same resource and either wait in queues or form circular wait-for cycles that the engine must break by aborting a victim transaction. This category covers both ordinary blocking chains and deadlocks because both share the lock manager as their root-cause locus. Observable phenomena: ungranted lock entries in lock-state catalogs and visible blocker-waiter chains, deadlock-detection reports and victim-rollback errors driving application retries, rising lock-wait time, declining transaction throughput, growing connection-pool wait queues, and application-level timeouts triggered by sustained blocking. Possible contributing factors: hot rows or counter columns updated by many concurrent sessions, long-running or uncommitted transactions, transactions held open across user interaction or external service calls, missing indexes that enlarge the lock footprint of a statement, overly strict transaction isolation levels, automatic lock-granularity escalation from row to page or table, online schema-change or metadata locks colliding with data modifications, and inconsistent resource-acquisition order across application code paths.

entry.official_definition: Terminates any session that has been idle within an open transaction for longer than the specified amount of time.
entry.trigger_condition: A session is idle, waiting for a client query, while an open transaction remains active longer than the configured threshold.
entry.workload_impact: The session is terminated; this prevents long idle transactions from holding locks or preventing vacuum cleanup.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
